subject: EUKONNECT deployment readiness — perf constraints, topology options, next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Aline Dupont <aline.dupont@eukonnect.io>, Sven Holm <sven.holm@eukonnect.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:18:00 +0100
Subject: Post-call recap: perf targets, model constraints, and next steps

Thanks for the call this morning — good discussion. Short recap and agreed next steps so we have a single reference. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared
- Production latency spikes under peak traffic (marketing campaign bursts) causing client timeouts and degraded UX.
- Inconsistent throughput when concurrent long-context sessions run and the KV cache is cold.
- Cost concerns for 24/7 dedicated capacity if the burst windows are relatively short.

Business goals / acceptance criteria
- Interactive chat latency target: p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 600ms for 2k token context (50% of workload).
- Background reranking jobs: throughput target 200 reqs/s sustained, occasional bursts to 600 reqs/s for 5-10 minutes.
- Maintain data isolation; EU data residency and support for customer-managed VPC connection.

Model & workload details we captured
- Primary model family: Llama2-13B variant (we discussed quantized 4-bit path) for chat.
- Typical context length: 2k-4k tokens; 10% of sessions exceed 3k tokens.
- 70% of requests are low-token chat; 30% are rerank/batch scoring.

Topology options we discussed
1) Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) + autoscale for bursts - predictable latency, higher baseline cost.
2) Private (VPC) deployment on your cloud account - meets compliance, gives control over networking and KMS.
3) Hosted hybrid - core low-latency traffic on dedicated, burst to hosted compatible model variants.

Redwood suggestions / short technical notes
- Recommended baseline for PoC: 4 x A10G-equivalent GPUs per zone for initial dedicated cluster; evaluate H100 if tight p99 under long contexts.
- KV cache warmup + prefix caching to reduce cold-cache tail latency; expect 30-40% token cost reduction for chat traffic once warm.
- Batch sizing: keep interactive max batch size = 8 with a small latency budget (10-15ms) to balance cost and p95.
- Canary approach: 2 zones, 10% traffic canary to validate latency under production mix.

Deliverables / next steps (owners + ETA)
- Redwood: share proposed topology diagram and SLO matrix (attached) by Fri 22 May. (Rishi)
- EUKONNECT: provide sample traces (1 hour of production traffic) and authentication contact for VPC setup. (Aline / IT)
- SE deep-dive call to validate GPU sizing and batching parameters next week. (Vivek to propose times)
- Contract & security: Laura to open an initial SOW draft and include SOC2/VPC requirements. (Laura)

Attachments included: eukonnect-proposed-topology-20260521.pdf (topology diagram), slo-matrix-eukonnect-20260521.csv (SLO baseline and cost assumptions)

Thanks again — very actionable call. I will send proposed times for the SE deep-dive separately.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Aline Dupont <aline.dupont@eukonnect.io>

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:03:12 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: perf targets, model constraints, and next steps

Thanks Rishi — this matches our notes. Two clarifications from our side:
1) Compliance: we need SOC2 Type II evidence and the ability to run in our VPC (we discussed bring-your-own-VPC). Is the private deployment package production-ready for our legal team review?
2) Canary window: can we target the week of 1 June for a 10% traffic canary? That timing aligns with our marketing campaign start.

We will collect the sample traces and send them to your SE. IT will be the contact for setting up VPC peering; copying our IT address so it lands with the right person.

Aline Dupont
Head of Product Operations, EUKONNECT
aline.dupont@eukonnect.io
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Aline Dupont <aline.dupont@eukonnect.io>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 10:12:45 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: perf targets, model constraints, and next steps

Quick technical notes and what I'll bring to the SE deep-dive:
- GPU guidance: A10G-equivalent is a cost-effective starting point for the 13B quantized model. If p99 under 4k context remains above 600ms in the PoC, we'll test 1x or 2x H100 nodes to compare tail behavior.
- Quantization tradeoffs: 4-bit quant gives ~2.5x throughput vs fp16 with modest quality impact. We'll run a small eval set (you can share preferred prompts) to verify.
- Batching: suggest interactive path with target latency budget 250ms; max_batch=8, batch_timeout=12ms. Rerank jobs go on a separate worker pool with larger batch sizes.
- Caching & warmup: implement prefix KV cache for repeated contexts and a small synthetic warmup during canary ramp to avoid cold-cache tail.
- Autoscaling policy: scale on p95 latency and GPU utilization; quick scale step to handle minute-level bursts is important for your campaign.

I'll prepare a test matrix and suggested k8s node types for the call. Proposed times for deep-dive: Tue 26 May 09:00-11:00 CET or Wed 27 May 14:00-16:00 CET. Which works for you?

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
